ORDER 1.

This Criminal Revision Petition has been filed by the revisionist/ complainant u/s 397 of the Code of Criminal Procedure assailing the impugned judgment dated 28.11.2018 passed by Ms. CR No.105/19 Gaurav Manchanda v. Sanjay Khanna Page 1of 4 Pryadarshani, Ld. MM01 (NI Act)
West District, Delhi, whereby the accused has been acquitted of committing offence u/s 138 of the Negotiable Instrument Act 1881 (as amended up to date) and (hereinafter referred as the N. I. Act.).
2.

3. Having heard the Ld. Counsel for the parties and on perusal of the record, without delving into the merits in the present revision, I find that the present revision is an appeal in disguise and not maintainable in terms of Section 378 (4) of Cr.P.C. that categorically provides that where an order of acquittal is passed in a case instituted upon a complaint, the complainant may prefer an appeal to the High Court, if a Special Leave for filing Appeal is granted by the High Court.

It is needless to point out that the power of the Court in case of Criminal Revision in terms of Section 397 Cr.P.C. is supervisory in nature and the same is not exercisable in case of a final judgment passed in terms of Section 353 Cr.P.C.

1 4.

sentences.text:
As regards the remedy of statutory appeal provided under Section 378(4) Cr.P.C., reliance can be placed on decision in Criminal Appeal No. 50 of 2013 titled Subhash Chand v. Delhi Administration,
dated 8th January 2013, wherein in relation to a complaint u/s Section 20 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, CR No.105/19 Gaurav Manchanda v. Sanjay Khanna Page 2of 4 which offences under the PFA Act are both cognizable and non cognizable.

entities.text: Criminal Appeal No. 50 of 2013 titled Subhash Chand v. Delhi Administration
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was observed:
"Thus, whether a case is a case instituted on a complaint depends on the legal provisions relating to the offence involved therein.

But once it is a case instituted on a complaint and an order of acquittal is passed, whether the offence be bailable or non bailable, cognizable or noncognizable, the complainant can file an application under Section 378(4) for special leave to appeal against it in the High Court.
Section 378(4) places no restriction on the complainant.

So far as the State is concerned, as per Section 378(1)(b), it can in any case, that is even in a case instituted on a complaint, direct the Public Prosecutor to file an appeal to the High Court from an original or appellate order of acquittal passed by any court other than High Court.
But there is, as stated by us hereinabove, an important inbuilt and categorical restriction on the State's power.
It cannot direct the Public Prosecutor to present an appeal from an order of acquittal passed by a Magistrate in respect of a cognizable and noncognizable offence.

In such a case the District Magistrate may under Section 378(1)
(a) direct the Public Prosecutor to file an appeal to the Session Court.

This appears to be the right approach and correct interpretation of Section 378 of the Code."
5.

Further, in Crl.A no. 972/2012 titled The Bhajanpura Cooperative Urban Thrift & Credit Society Ltd. v. Sushil Kumar decided on 3 September, 2014 by the High Court of Delhi, it was observed that "the remedy available to the complainants under Section 138 N.I.Act against order of acquittal is only to seek special leave before filing an appeal under Section 378 (4) Cr.P.C. before the High Court".

sentences.text: No case law has been cited by the Ld. Counsel for the revisionist to the contrary despite affording an opportunity.
There is no gainsaying that the Court has wider powers when exercising appellate jurisdiction in case a final judgment is assailed by a party while the revisionary jurisdiction is a limited one.
Therefore, since the impugned judgment dated 28.11.2018 is a final order, no revision lies before this Court as appropriate remedy is to file an appeal.
This Court does not have jurisdiction to adjudicate upon the matter in revision.
Hence, same is dismissed.
7. The Trial Court Record alongwith copy of this order be sent back to the Court concerned.
The Revision Petition file be consigned to Record Room.
